subject: Bernard Francis "Solanus" Casey, O.F.M. Cap.

milestones.title: Born on a Wisconsin farm
milestones.body: Bernard Francis Casey — "Barney" — is born the sixth of sixteen children to Irish immigrants Bernard James Casey and Ellen Elizabeth Murphy on a farm near the St. Croix River. Two of his sisters will die of diphtheria in a single month in 1878.

milestones.title: A late, uncertain start at seminary
milestones.place: St. Francis de Sales Seminary, Milwaukee
milestones.body: After work as a logger, hospital orderly, streetcar motorman and prison guard, Barney enters the diocesan seminary at Milwaukee. His Latin and German falter; he is advised he would do better in a religious order.

milestones.title: Receives the Capuchin habit — and the name Solanus
milestones.body: He enters the Capuchin novitiate in Detroit and is invested with the brown habit, taking the name Solanus after the Spanish missionary St. Francis Solanus. He professes his vows the following year.

milestones.title: Ordained a 'simplex priest'
milestones.place: St. Francis of Assisi Church, Milwaukee
milestones.body: Solanus is ordained — but as a sacerdos simplex: he may celebrate Mass but is not entrusted to preach doctrinal sermons or hear confessions. The restriction will shape, and never diminish, a fifty-year ministry.

milestones.title: Doorkeeper in Yonkers
milestones.place: Sacred Heart Parish, Yonkers, New York
milestones.body: His first assignment: porter and sacristan at Sacred Heart. Word spreads of the quiet priest at the door whose blessings and counsel seem to be followed by healings. The earliest letters in this archive date from these years.

milestones.title: The tenement parishes of New York
milestones.place: Our Lady Queen of Angels, Harlem, New York
milestones.body: Transferred to Our Lady of Sorrows and then Our Lady Queen of Angels in Manhattan and Harlem, Solanus keeps the door and enrolls the sick and troubled in the Seraphic Mass Association. The notebooks of reported favors begin.

milestones.title: Porter of St. Bonaventure, Detroit
milestones.body: He returns to Detroit as doorkeeper — the post he will hold for twenty-one years. People come by the hundreds; the monastery notebooks fill with names, ailments, petitions, and the favors said to follow.

milestones.title: Feeding the Depression's hungry
milestones.body: As the Depression deepens, Solanus helps found the Capuchin Soup Kitchen, which feeds thousands of Detroiters daily. It is still operating today.

milestones.title: Persuaded to write his memoirs
milestones.body: Now in his seventies and worn by decades at the door, Solanus is encouraged to set down recollections of his life and of the favors he has witnessed.

milestones.title: A quieter house in Huntington
milestones.body: For his health, Solanus is transferred to the friary at Huntington. Even in semi-retirement the letters and visitors follow him.

milestones.title: Death in Detroit
milestones.body: Solanus dies at 86, his last words a renewal of the offering that defined him: "I give my soul to Jesus Christ." An estimated 20,000 people file past his body at St. Bonaventure.

milestones.title: Declared Venerable
milestones.body: Pope John Paul II recognizes the heroic virtue of Fr. Solanus Casey, naming him Venerable — the first American-born man so honored.

milestones.title: Beatified before 60,000
milestones.body: Following a medically inexplicable healing attributed to his intercession, Fr. Solanus Casey is beatified at Ford Field in Detroit before a crowd of some 60,000 — now Blessed Solanus Casey.
